Looking at this question about nanobody mutations targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD, I need to consider which mutation in the CDR2 region would pull the loop closer to the RBD in computational models.

The key consideration is the structural effect of each mutation:
- G56H replaces a glycine (smallest amino acid, no side chain, high flexibility) with a histidine (larger, polar side chain)
- This substitution would reduce local flexibility and introduce steric bulk at position 56
- In computational models, this change in the CDR2 loop would alter the loop conformation, pulling it closer to the RBD surface

The Glycine to Histidine substitution at position 56 is the mutation that, in computational studies of this nanobody-RBD complex, was shown to reposition the CDR2 loop to be in closer proximity to the RBD.

[ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
